title: Arroz con Leche: Stovetop Rice Pudding with Cinnamon and Lemon Zest
description: Long-grain rice simmered first in water with a cinnamon stick and lemon peel, then slowly in milk until creamy. A Latin American pantry dessert that feeds six from a few cups of milk and a handful of rice.
notes: Stir more often as the pudding thickens, since milk scorches easily on the bottom of a thin pan. Take it off the heat while it still looks a little loose; the rice keeps absorbing milk and it firms up a good deal as it cools. If leftovers set too thick, stir in a splash of milk before serving cold or warming gently. Unsweetened nut-free plant milk works in place of whole milk and makes it dairy-free, though it will be less rich; if you use soy milk, the recipe then contains soy. Refrigerate within 2 hours in a covered container and eat within 4 days. Rice pudding does not freeze well, as the rice turns grainy.

ingredients.name: wide strips of lemon zest, removed with a vegetable peeler

instructions: Rinse the rice in a fine strainer under cold water for about 30 seconds, until the water runs mostly clear, and drain well.

In a heavy 3-quart saucepan, combine the rice, water, cinnamon stick, lemon zest strips and salt. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then lower the heat to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring once or twice, until nearly all the water is absorbed and the rice is just tender at the edges.
Pour in the milk and sugar and stir well. Bring back to a bare simmer over medium heat, then turn the heat to medium-low so the surface just trembles.

Simmer for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring every few minutes and scraping the bottom and corners, until the rice is soft and the pudding is creamy and loose, like thick oatmeal. If using raisins, stir them in for the last 5 minutes so they plump.
Remove from the heat. Fish out the cinnamon stick and lemon zest and stir in the vanilla.
Serve warm, or spoon into bowls, press plastic wrap onto the surface and refrigerate for at least 2 hours to serve cold. Dust each bowl with ground cinnamon just before serving.

title: Kheer: Cardamom Rice Pudding with Basmati and Raisins
description: A small amount of ghee-toasted basmati rice cooked low and slow in milk until the milk reduces and turns creamy, then sweetened and scented with cardamom. Nut-free as written, with raisins on top if you like.
notes: Kheer is meant to have far more milk than rice; the slow reduction is what makes it rich, so resist the urge to add more rice. A wide, heavy pot reduces the milk faster and is less likely to scorch; if a brown film forms on the bottom, do not scrape it up, just pour the kheer into a clean pot. Sliced almonds or pistachios are a traditional garnish, but they add tree nuts, so leave them off for a nut-free kitchen. A small pinch of saffron steeped in a spoonful of warm milk can be added with the sugar. Kheer thickens a great deal in the refrigerator, so loosen cold leftovers with a few tablespoons of milk. Refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 3 days; it does not freeze well.
instructions: Rinse the rice in a fine-mesh strainer until the water runs clear, then cover with fresh water and soak for 20 minutes. Drain well and pat dry on a towel.
Melt the ghee in a heavy-bottomed 4-quart pot over medium heat. Add the drained rice and stir for 1 to 2 minutes, until the grains look glossy and smell lightly toasted.
Pour in the milk and bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring often so it does not catch. As soon as it rises, lower the heat to medium-low.

Simmer gently for 40 to 45 minutes, stirring and scraping the bottom every 3 to 4 minutes and stirring any skin back in, until the rice is very soft and breaking apart and the milk has reduced by about a third and looks creamy.
Stir in the sugar, cardamom, salt and raisins, if using, and simmer 5 minutes more, until the sugar dissolves and the raisins plump. The kheer should coat a spoon but still pour.
Serve warm, or cool, cover and refrigerate for at least 3 hours to serve chilled, the way it is often eaten in summer.

title: Tres Leches Cake with Whipped Cream and Cinnamon
description: A light sponge baked in a 9x13 pan, soaked overnight in evaporated, condensed and whole milk, and topped with softly whipped cream. Fifteen generous squares from pantry cans and five eggs.
notes: Separate the eggs while cold and let them warm up; the whites must go into a completely clean, grease-free bowl or they will not whip. Fold gently so the batter keeps its air, because the open sponge is what drinks up the milk without turning soggy. Pour the soak in three or four rounds and give each a few minutes to sink in; it may look like too much at first, but it all absorbs overnight. This is a dairy cake and must stay refrigerated: never leave it out more than 2 hours, and keep it covered in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Do not freeze it once soaked. You can bake the sponge a day ahead, wrap it in the pan and soak it the next morning.

ingredients.name: large eggs, separated, at room temperature

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the center. Grease the bottom and sides of a 9x13-inch baking pan. In a small bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder and salt.
In a large bowl, beat the egg yolks with 3/4 cup of the sugar on high speed for about 2 minutes, until pale yellow and thick. Beat in the 1/3 cup whole milk and 1 teaspoon of the vanilla on low.

In a second clean bowl with clean beaters, beat the egg whites on medium-high until foamy and opaque. Sprinkle in the remaining 1/4 cup sugar a spoonful at a time and keep beating until the whites hold stiff, glossy peaks, 2 to 3 minutes.

Sift or sprinkle the flour mixture over the yolk mixture and fold it in with a spatula until no dry streaks remain. Fold in one third of the whites to loosen the batter, then gently fold in the rest in two additions, stopping as soon as no white streaks show.

Spread the batter evenly in the pan. Bake for 22 to 26 minutes, until the top is golden, springs back when pressed, and a toothpick in the center comes out clean. Cool in the pan on a rack for 30 minutes.

Whisk the evaporated milk, sweetened condensed milk and 1/4 cup whole milk together in a large measuring cup. Poke holes all over the warm cake with a fork or skewer, about every half inch, going all the way to the bottom.

Pour the milk mixture over the cake in three or four rounds, waiting a few minutes between each and paying attention to the edges and corners. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight, until the milk is absorbed.

Before serving, beat the cold heavy cream with the powdered sugar and remaining 1 teaspoon vanilla to soft, billowy peaks. Spread it over the chilled cake, dust with cinnamon and cut into 15 squares. Serve cold.

title: Chè Chuối-Style Vietnamese Banana and Coconut Tapioca Pudding
description: Ripe banana chunks simmered in a lightly salted coconut milk and small pearl tapioca pudding until soft and glossy. A vegan Vietnamese-style sweet soup made from a can, a few bananas and a little sugar.
notes: Use bananas that are yellow with a few brown freckles but still firm, so the chunks hold their shape; very soft bananas melt into the pudding. The salt matters here, since it keeps the coconut sweetness in balance. Small pearl tapioca is done when the pearls are clear with only a tiny white dot left in the center, and they finish cooking as the pudding sits. In Vietnam this is often topped with crushed roasted peanuts and toasted sesame seeds; add them at the table if you like, but they add peanuts and sesame to the allergens. The pudding thickens a lot as it cools, so loosen leftovers with a few tablespoons of hot water. Refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 3 days, warmed gently or at room temperature; it does not freeze well.

ingredients.name: ripe banana, firm with a few brown spots (about 1 1/2 lb unpeeled)
full-fat coconut milk (13.5 oz), shaken well

instructions: Peel the bananas, halve them lengthwise and cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces. In a medium bowl, toss them with the sugar and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt and let stand for 20 minutes, until the sugar dissolves into a light syrup.
Meanwhile, rinse the tapioca in a fine strainer, then soak it in a bowl of cool water for 15 minutes. Drain.

Bring the 2 1/2 cups water to a boil in a 3-quart saucepan. Stir in the drained tapioca, lower the heat to medium-low and simmer for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring often so the pearls do not stick, until they are mostly translucent.

Set aside 1/4 cup of the coconut milk for serving. Stir the rest into the pot with the remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt and bring back to a gentle simmer; do not let it boil hard or the coconut milk may separate.

Add the bananas and all their syrup. Simmer gently for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring carefully, until the bananas are soft at the edges and slightly translucent and the pudding coats a spoon. Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla, if using.
Let stand 5 minutes, then ladle into bowls warm or at room temperature and drizzle each with a little of the reserved coconut milk.

title: Greek-Style Yogurt with Honey, Toasted Walnuts and Cinnamon
description: Thick whole-milk yogurt topped with skillet-toasted walnuts glazed in honey and cinnamon, then a final drizzle of honey. A no-oven dessert ready in about 15 minutes, in the spirit of the Greek yiaourti me meli.
notes: Watch the walnuts closely; they go from toasted to bitter in under a minute, so pull them as soon as they smell nutty. The honey glaze turns crisp only once the nuts cool, so spread them out rather than leaving them in a pile. Do not give honey to babies under 12 months old. For a nut-free version, use raw pumpkin seeds or sunflower seeds in place of walnuts, which removes the tree nut allergen. A spoonful of diced apple or a little lemon zest on top is a good addition. The glazed walnuts keep airtight at room temperature for 1 week; assemble the bowls just before serving, and keep the yogurt refrigerated, never left out more than 2 hours.

ingredients.name: plain whole-milk greek yogurt (about 680 g), cold

instructions: Line a plate with parchment. Toast the walnuts in a dry 10-inch skillet over medium-low heat for 5 to 6 minutes, shaking the pan often, until they are a shade darker and smell nutty.
Add 1 tablespoon of the honey, 1/2 teaspoon of the cinnamon and the salt. Stir constantly for 30 to 60 seconds, until the honey bubbles and coats the nuts in a sticky glaze.
Scrape the walnuts onto the parchment and spread them out. Let cool for at least 5 minutes, until the glaze sets and the nuts feel crisp, then break up any clumps.
Spoon about 1/2 cup yogurt into each of 6 bowls and swirl the back of the spoon through it to make a hollow. Drizzle each with about 2 teaspoons of the remaining honey.
Scatter the glazed walnuts over the top, dust with the remaining 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon and add a little lemon zest, if using. Serve right away, while the nuts are still crunchy.

title: Old-Fashioned Stovetop Chocolate Pudding (No Eggs)
description: Cocoa, sugar and cornstarch whisked into whole milk and cooked until thick and glossy, finished with butter and vanilla. A from-scratch pudding with no eggs, made in one saucepan in about 15 minutes.
notes: Whisking the dry ingredients together before any milk goes in is what keeps the cornstarch and cocoa from clumping. The pudding must bubble for a full minute; undercooked cornstarch tastes chalky and can thin out in the refrigerator. After chilling, stir gently rather than whisking hard, since heavy beating breaks a cornstarch set. For a dairy-free and vegan pudding, use unsweetened nut-free plant milk and swap the butter for coconut oil; the set is a little softer, and soy milk would add soy to the allergens. Press plastic onto the surface to prevent a skin, or skip it if your family fights over the skin. Refrigerate within 2 hours, covered, for up to 4 days; it does not freeze well.
instructions: In a medium heavy saucepan, off the heat, whisk together the sugar, cocoa, cornstarch and salt until evenly colored with no lumps of cocoa left.
Whisk in 1/2 cup of the milk to make a smooth, thick paste, scraping the corners of the pan with a spatula. Then whisk in the remaining 2 1/4 cups milk until smooth.
Set the pan over medium heat and cook, whisking constantly and reaching into the edges, for 7 to 9 minutes, until the mixture steams, begins to thicken and the first large bubbles break the surface.
Keep whisking while it bubbles gently for 1 full minute. It should be thick and glossy and leave a clear trail when you draw a spatula across the bottom of the pan.
Remove from the heat and whisk in the butter and vanilla until melted and smooth. For the silkiest texture, pour it through a fine strainer.

Divide among 4 small bowls. Press plastic wrap directly onto each surface if you do not want a skin, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours, until cold and set. It can also be eaten warm, when it is softer and saucier.

title: Vegan Baked Cinnamon Apples with Oat Filling
description: Whole apples cored and packed with a brown sugar, cinnamon and oat filling made with coconut oil, then baked until tender with their own syrupy pan juices. One apple per person, vegan and gluten-free.
notes: Choose firm apples that hold their shape when baked, such as Honeycrisp, Braeburn, Jonagold or Granny Smith; soft eating apples like Red Delicious collapse. Peeling a strip around the top lets steam escape so the skins do not split. The apples are done when a paring knife slides into the thickest part with no resistance. Unsalted butter can replace the coconut oil, but then the recipe contains milk and is no longer vegan. Use certified gluten-free oats if anyone needs the recipe gluten-free, since regular oats are often cross-contaminated with wheat. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours for up to 4 days and rewarm in the microwave for 1 to 2 minutes, until hot through.

ingredients.name: medium firm baking apple, such as Honeycrisp or Braeburn
certified gluten-free old-fashioned rolled oats (45 g)

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F with a rack in the center.

Core each apple from the stem end with a melon baller or small spoon, leaving the bottom 1/2 inch intact so the filling cannot leak out. Widen the opening to about 1 1/2 inches and scoop out every seed. Peel a 1-inch strip of skin from around the top of each apple.
In a small bowl, stir together the oats, brown sugar, melted coconut oil, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt and raisins, if using, until the oats are evenly moistened and clump slightly.
Stand the apples in an 8-inch square baking dish and pack the filling into the hollows, mounding the extra on top. Pour the water into the dish around the apples and cover the dish tightly with foil.

Bake covered for 25 minutes. Uncover, spoon some of the pan liquid over the apples, and bake uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes more, until the topping is browned and a paring knife slides easily into the apples.
Let the apples rest in the dish for 10 minutes, then serve warm with the syrupy pan juices spooned over each one.

title: Chocolate Banana Nice Cream from Frozen Bananas
description: Frozen ripe bananas blended with cocoa, a little maple syrup and plant milk until they turn into soft-serve. No cooking, no ice cream maker, and a good use for bananas that are about to go too far.
notes: Plan ahead: the banana slices need at least 6 hours in the freezer, and a bag of them kept in the freezer means dessert is always 10 minutes away. The riper and more freckled the bananas, the sweeter the result, so you may need less maple syrup. The mixture goes through a crumbly stage before it turns smooth; keep processing and add liquid only a tablespoon at a time, or it turns into a smoothie. A high-powered blender works but needs a little more liquid and the tamper. Stirring in a spoonful of natural creamy peanut butter is good, but it adds peanuts and the recipe is no longer nut-free. Leftovers freeze hard; let them sit at room temperature for 10 to 15 minutes before scooping, and eat within 1 week.

ingredients.name: ripe banana, peeled, sliced 1/2 inch thick and frozen (about 450 g peeled)
unsweetened nut-free plant milk, plus more as needed

instructions: At least 6 hours ahead, spread the banana slices in a single layer on a parchment-lined rimmed baking sheet so they do not freeze into a block. Freeze until solid, then transfer to a freezer bag if not using right away.
Let the frozen slices sit on the counter for 5 minutes. Put them in a food processor with the cocoa, maple syrup, vanilla, salt and 2 tablespoons of the plant milk.
Pulse about 10 times to break the bananas into coarse crumbs, then run the processor for 2 to 4 minutes, stopping to scrape down the sides every minute.
Add more plant milk a tablespoon at a time only if the blades are spinning without catching. Stop when the mixture suddenly turns smooth, glossy and creamy, like soft-serve.
Serve right away for soft-serve, or scrape into a loaf pan or container, cover and freeze for 1 to 2 hours for a firmer, scoopable texture.

title: Vegan No-Bake Chocolate Peanut Butter Oat Cookies
description: The stovetop drop cookie many grew up on, made with coconut oil and oat milk: a cocoa sugar syrup boiled for one minute, stirred with peanut butter and oats, and left to set. No oven, about 30 cookies.
notes: The 1-minute boil is everything: start timing only once the whole surface is bubbling and keeps bubbling as you stir. Too short a boil and the cookies stay soft and sticky; too long and they set dry and crumbly. If a batch will not firm up, press it into a parchment-lined 8-inch pan, chill until set and cut into bars. Old-fashioned oats give a chewy cookie; for a tighter, more classic texture, pulse 1 cup of the oats a few times in a food processor first. Unsalted butter and whole milk can replace the coconut oil and oat milk, which adds milk to the allergens. Sunflower seed butter works for a peanut-free version. Coconut oil softens in a warm room, so store the cookies airtight in the refrigerator for up to 1 week, or freeze for up to 2 months.

ingredients.name: natural creamy peanut butter, well stirred (130 g)
certified gluten-free old-fashioned rolled oats (270 g)

instructions: Line 2 rimmed baking sheets with parchment. Measure the peanut butter, vanilla and oats and set them beside the stove, because the mixture sets quickly once it comes off the heat.
In a 3-quart saucepan, combine the sugar, coconut oil, oat milk, cocoa and salt. Cook over medium heat, stirring, for 3 to 5 minutes, until the oil melts and the sugar dissolves.
Bring the mixture to a full rolling boil, with bubbles across the entire surface that do not die down when stirred. Set a timer and boil for exactly 1 minute, stirring only occasionally.
Remove the pan from the heat. Stir in the peanut butter and vanilla until smooth, then add the oats and stir until every flake is coated.
Working quickly, drop heaping tablespoons onto the lined sheets about 1 inch apart and nudge each into a round with the back of the spoon.
Let the cookies set at room temperature for 30 to 45 minutes, or in the refrigerator for 15 minutes, until they are firm and lift cleanly off the parchment.

title: Mexican-Style Chocolate Crinkle Cookies with Cinnamon and Cayenne
description: Fudgy cocoa cookies rolled in powdered sugar so they crack white as they bake, warmed with cinnamon and a pinch of cayenne. Made with oil, not butter, at under 15 cents a cookie.
notes: The dough is very soft at first and must chill until firm, at least 2 hours, or the cookies spread and the sugar coating dissolves. Rolling in granulated sugar before the powdered sugar keeps the coating bright white instead of soaking in. Pull the cookies while the centers still look soft between the cracks; they firm up on the sheet and stay fudgy. The cayenne gives gentle warmth at the back of the throat; leave it out for small children or double it for more heat. Dutch-process cocoa also works and gives a darker cookie. Do not taste the raw dough, which contains raw egg and flour. Store airtight at room temperature for up to 5 days, or freeze the uncoated dough balls for up to 3 months and roll them in sugar after they thaw slightly.

ingredients.name: high-heat neutral oil, such as canola (55 g)

instructions: In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, cinnamon, cayenne and salt.

In a large bowl, whisk the cocoa, 1 cup granulated sugar and oil until evenly combined; it will look like damp sand. Whisk in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla, and keep whisking for about 30 seconds, until the mixture is glossy and smooth.
Stir the flour mixture into the cocoa mixture with a spatula just until no dry streaks remain. The dough will be soft and sticky, like thick brownie batter.
Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or up to 2 days, until the dough is firm enough to roll.
Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the center and line 2 rimmed baking sheets with parchment. Put the 2 tablespoons granulated sugar and the powdered sugar in two separate shallow bowls.

Scoop level tablespoons of dough and roll them quickly between your palms into balls. Roll each in the granulated sugar, then coat it heavily in the powdered sugar, and set 12 on each sheet about 2 inches apart.
Bake one sheet at a time for 10 to 12 minutes, until the cookies have puffed and spread, the tops are deeply cracked and the edges are set, but the centers still look soft in the cracks.
Cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool completely. Keep the second sheet of dough balls in the refrigerator while the first one bakes.
